why: Barely, but yes. The first line '假如说，你是圆明园的马首' puts me inside a thing, which is odd enough to hold me for a few seconds, and 圆明园 is a word I know from school so I want to see where it goes. The picture is polished: a glowing horse head in a spotlight, with nice colors. But 0:00-0:03 is one static shot and I don't yet know why I should care. What actually keeps my thumb off the screen is that at 0:03.6 the scene changes (1860 smoke), then at 0:05.9 a London auction with a gavel, then Hong Kong, Beijing and home, one new scene every 2-4 seconds. Without that fast montage I would have gone at about 4s.
first_moment_I_got_curious: 0:05.87-0:10 (London auction, then HK 'LOT HK$ 1094万 -> 6910万' ticking up, 又被人花6910万买下) made me think 'a statue is bought for that much?'. The real hook is 0:14.93 '可十二个里，还有五个没回来' with the row of 12 zodiac arches and the dashed empty outlines. That is when I understood this is a whole set and 5 are still missing. At 0:18.17 the title card '马首回家，用了160年' gave me the question: why 160 years?
where_I_would_swipe_away: 0:26-0:34 the fountain and 水力钟 explanation: about 8s of nearly the same wide shot of a pool with little new information. If I am not already hooked, I leave here. It does pay off at 0:34.7 when all 12 spout at once.

1:06.4-1:09.4 the handshake silhouettes and the name 何鸿燊, who I don't know. This is the 4th time the same two-silhouette handshake or handover image appears (0:10, 1:06, 1:33, 1:39), so it feels like clip-art repeating and I stop paying attention.

1:44-1:56 is the most likely swipe point. The sofa and window scene holds 7s on '他没等到，你回家那天。', then a truck drives across a night road for about 6s while the subtitle sits unfinished on '2020年12月1日，'. Nothing changes except the sky color, the truck's '小心轻放' label is too small to read on a phone, and the sentence only completes at 1:56 '你回到圆明园'. The sofa beat is emotional, but the truck beat is a stall.

2:08-2:17 the 正觉寺 red-gate building (not mentioned again) and then 9s on the horse's ear 'curled' detail. It feels like a side trip right when the story should be ending. I swipe around 2:14 if I'm tired.
General: a 2:34 landscape video on Douyin is long. Subtitles top-left are small, and tiny labels (国家文物局：主张终止公开拍卖, 保利4·国博2, the source line) are unreadable on a phone.
frames_I_did_not_understand: 0:03.60-0:05.47: the horse head sits on top of a headless robed body in front of blurry grey oval blobs (smoke? a crowd? heads?). At 0:05.0 the head floats up out of frame and the headless robe stays, which looks strange. I only half get it as 'being taken away'.

0:08-0:10: the ticking 'LOT HK$ 1094万 -> 2791万 -> 6873万 -> 6910万' shows a real public bidding war ending at 6910万. Later, 1:10-1:20 says the hammer did NOT fall in 2007 and he bought it privately beforehand for 6910万. Those two pictures contradict each other, and I wondered which one is true.

0:17.37-0:17.93: a fast rewind with glitch lines through 2003, 1908, 1892, 1861, 1845, 1814, with a 'LOT HK$ 5831万' sign. It flashes by in 0.5s. I couldn't read it, and 1908/1892 prices make no sense to me. It just feels like a flicker.
0:18.17-0:20.77: the title card has no subtitle line for about 3s. It looks fine, but there is a gap in the voice-over/subtitle rhythm.
0:25.00-0:25.13: the first Haiyantang close-up. The animal heads sit on robed bodies at a skewed angle like a stack, and I can't tell what I'm looking at until the wide shot at 0:26.

0:33.00: the label '水力钟' overlaps the '在家 12/12' counter (ghosted text over text). 0:33.40-0:34.33: the zoomed frame doesn't fill the screen, with a dark navy band on the right and bottom. It looks like a glitch.

0:40.40-0:48: the soldiers are silhouettes walking in front of the statues and overlapping them. I can't see any fire at 0:43.8-0:48 '一把火', only a brown haze behind the building, so 放火 is only in the text, not in the picture. The vase one carries looks like it floats in front of his chest.

0:48.33-0:52: the counter goes 12 -> 10 -> 2 -> 0 in about 3s, but at '在家 2' I can still see about 4-5 animal heads on the statues, so number and picture don't match. The label also changes from '在家' to '回国 0/12'. Also a navy border appears around the close-up again.

0:59.67-1:06: the 牛、猴、虎 are three brown lumps on the table. I can't tell which is which, and I can't tell who paddle 23/41/17 are or who bought them. Same for 鼠 and 兔 at 1:25-1:35: brown blobs, the rat doesn't look like a rat.
1:21.73-1:24.73: the bar chart jumps from 6910万港元 to '884万美元' and the 1989 bar is labeled '几十万美元'. Different currency and a vague number, so I can't check '二十多倍' myself.
1:37.00-1:39.43: the visitors' silhouettes walk across the pedestal and cover the horse head, and at 1:38.21 two of them merge into one tangled body. It looks like an animation glitch.

1:42.67-1:50: a glowing orange dot in the window at night. Is it a star, a lamp, a firework? Unexplained. '他' also isn't named in the subtitle at that point, so I only know it's 何鸿燊 from the small top-right text.

2:08-2:11: the translucent orange triangles beside the red wall and the grey jagged shapes. Flames and rubble? I only guess. '正觉寺' is also a name I don't know, and the horse head isn't in the picture.

2:11.53-2:17.60: the subtitle says '一只耳朵卷了', but the drawn ears look straight and undamaged. The circle highlights an ear that looks perfectly normal, and the head is cropped at the jaw. I can't see what 'curled' or '撞过' means.

2:22-2:26: the 11 other statues are now grey and headless in a different layout, with faint dashed heads overlapping the water arcs. The counters ('保利4·国博2', '回国7 / 回家1') are tiny. The words 回国 and 回家 are used differently (in China vs back in the garden), which I only got from 2:06 '回到圆明园的，只有你'.
2:27-2:30: the dashed 'dragon head' ghost with a '?' looks like rabbit ears, so I thought of the rabbit. The line '真假说不清' has no follow-up and then the video ends.
takeaway_in_my_words: The 圆明园 horse head, one of 12 zodiac water-spout heads, was looted in 1860, then spent 160 years being auctioned and traded around the world (London, HK, private deals, a donation) before getting back to 圆明园 in 2020. Only 7 of the 12 are back in China, only the horse is back in the garden, and 5 are still missing. Each 'return' cost huge money or luck, and then the video asks me whether we should pay to buy more back.
surprise_that_stuck: That these animal heads were not decoration but spouts of a water clock: every 2 hours the one whose turn it was sprayed, and at noon all 12 sprayed together. The horse was literally the noon one. A second one was the 3149万欧元 sale in Paris where the buyer then refused to pay (the red '未付款' stamp). Third, the 6910万 price versus a few hundred thousand dollars 18 years before ('二十多倍').
what_I_would_comment: 评论1: '花6910万买回来被抢走的东西，是不是等于告诉别人抢了能卖钱？' 评论2: '何鸿燊98岁没等到马首回家那天，看到这里鼻子酸了。' 评论3: '12个里还差5个，龙蛇羊鸡狗在哪啊，2018年法国那个到底是不是真的？' 评论4: '最后一问我选不买，但是民间捐的呢？'

for_frames_only.what_this_says_in_5s: A dark teal room, a big terracotta horse head on a white block under a spotlight, the sentence '假如说，你是圆明园的马首。' appearing at top-left, '2026 · 圆明园 正觉寺·文殊亭' top-right. I read it as a museum object and a 'you are the horse' storytelling gimmick. Pretty, but nothing moves yet and I don't know the stakes.

A rewind glitch ends on the smoky 1814 scene, then a flat blue card with a big white title '马首回家，用了160年' and a small horse head icon. Reads instantly as the thesis: it took 160 years to get home. I think 'wait, so how, and why so long?'. There is no subtitle for the next 3 seconds.

A cream European palace behind a turquoise pool, 12 animal-head statues on both sides all shooting white water arcs to the middle, subtitle '正午十二点，十二个一起喷水。', '12:00 · 午时' top-right, and '在家 12/12' bottom-left. It reads as a fancy fountain with a clock theme, and it's the prettiest and most surprising picture in the video.

A dark blue 2007 Hong Kong auction room: the auctioneer's hammer raised and frozen, a 'LOT — — —' sign, paddles 23 and 41 up, the horse head glowing on the table, subtitle '这一次，锤子没有落下。'. I get 'the sale was stopped at the last moment', though the small line about 国家文物局 can't be read on a phone and contradicts the 0:08 auction that did reach 6910万.

A dusk road with trees and a small grey truck driving right with its headlight on, subtitle '2020年12月1日，' still unfinished. I guess the horse is in the truck being delivered, but the '小心轻放' is too tiny, nothing is happening, and I'd start to swipe. At 1:56.27 it cuts to the pavilion on a green field and the sentence finishes with '你回到圆明园。'.

Blue sky, trees, ruins, and the horse head in a small green-roofed pavilion on a grass field, subtitle '十二个里，回到中国的有七个。', counter '回国 7/12'. Peaceful and calm, it reads as 'home at last', though the line before it was about 'seven are back' so it's slightly repeated; one second later two museum icons appear with '只有你'.

A purple-blue auction room with an empty white table and a dashed ghost head with a '?' over it, auctioneer at right, subtitle '2018年，法国拍出疑似龙首：真假说不清。'. I get 'another head turned up in France but may be fake'. It's a question mark, not an answer, and a half-second later the end card '如果找到了，该花钱买回来吗？' appears.

title_note: Not requested for this gate; nothing else added.
